name: manual_495096
claim: After 'gh pr merge' on any branch other than main (a stacked/dependent PR whose base is a feature branch), immediately git fetch that branch and reconcile the local checkout before doing any further local work on it. gh pr merge updates the branch on GitHub only -- a local checkout of that same branch does not auto-update, and continuing local merges (e.g. pulling in main) can silently operate on the stale pre-merge file content with no error and no conflict marker, quietly reverting a fix that appears to have already landed.

decisions.notes: 2026-07-23: merged a stacked PR via gh pr merge (base was a feature branch, not main), then continued doing local git merge operations on that same branch's LOCAL checkout without ever fetching the remote's new tip. A subsequent 'sync main' merge silently carried forward the stale, pre-fix version of a file -- no conflict, no error -- and the regression only surfaced later when an unrelated test started failing for a reason that traced back to a missing function. Root-caused via git log -- <file> showing the fix commit wasn't in local history at all, then git fetch + git rev-parse confirming local and origin had diverged. Also codified in orama-system's git-history-surgery skill (Non-Negotiables + a new 'Absorbing external/automated PR content' section: sync all remotes FIRST, replay new/adapted content LAST, never interleaved).
